steps.name: QC and limma-trend differential expression, treated vs control
steps.context: Input is log_expr.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples, log2(TPM+1) values as delivered by the core facility) and metadata.csv (12 samples x 2 columns, one row per sample with condition treated/control). Design is 6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch — no batch correction term is needed. Because values are pre-normalized log2 expression rather than raw counts, count-based DE tools (DESeq2, edgeR, pyDESeq2) are not appropriate; limma's moderated t-test with the intensity-dependent trend option (limma-trend, per Ritchie et al. 2015 Nucleic Acids Research) is the correct model for this data type.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 profiled genes differ in expression between the 6 treated and 6 control muscle samples, given that the input is already log2(TPM+1) normalized (not raw counts)?

grounding.reason: limma-trend (lmFit + eBayes(trend=TRUE) on pre-normalized log-expression, no voom) is the method recommended by Ritchie ME et al., 'limma powers differential expression analyses for RNA-sequencing and microarray studies', Nucleic Acids Research 2015 (PMID 25605792), for data delivered as log-expression rather than raw counts.

acceptance_criteria: Sample-metadata join confirms exactly 6 treated and 6 control samples matching the profiled design; any mismatch is reported explicitly, not silently resolved
PCA and sample-sample correlation plots are produced from the filtered log2 matrix to check for outlier samples or unexpected substructure
Low-expressed genes are filtered using an explicit, stated threshold on the log2(TPM+1) matrix before model fitting, and the number of genes retained is reported
limma lmFit + eBayes(trend=TRUE) is fit on the filtered log2 expression matrix with a treated-vs-control design matrix (no voom step, since input is not counts)
Full topTable output (logFC, AveExpr, moderated t, P.Value, BH-adjusted P.Value) is written for all tested genes, plus a separate list of genes passing adj.P.Val < 0.05
A volcano plot and a heatmap of the top differentially expressed genes are produced
The report explicitly states the data are pre-normalized log2 values (not counts) and that this is why limma-trend rather than DESeq2/edgeR was used

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of treated-vs-control DE genes
steps.context: Consumes the limma DE table from T1S1 (logFC, t-statistic, adj.P.Val per gene). Uses organism-matched pathway gene sets confirmed present in the environment: WikiPathways human (2026.07.10 snapshot, HGNC symbols), MSigDB Hallmark human (2026.1, 50 sets, HGNC symbols), and Reactome pathways (current GMT, filtered to Homo sapiens via the accompanying pathway index/species column, since the Reactome GMT covers all species in one file). Gene identifiers in the expression matrix must be checked and, if not already HGNC symbols, mapped via org.Hs.eg.db before matching to these gene sets.
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control muscle samples?

grounding.reason: Standard ORA+GSEA pathway enrichment workflow against curated gene-set collections; no disputed methodological rule applies, choice of WikiPathways/Hallmark/Reactome is dictated by what is confirmed present in the environment for Homo sapiens.

acceptance_criteria: Gene identifier type in the DE table is verified against the gene-set identifier type (HGNC symbol) and mapped via org.Hs.eg.db if needed, with the number of unmapped genes reported

Over-representation analysis (ORA) is run separately on up- and down-regulated significant gene sets (adj.P.Val < 0.05) against WikiPathways human, MSigDB Hallmark human, and Reactome (human-filtered) gene sets
Rank-based GSEA (fgsea) is run on the full ranked gene list (ranked by moderated t-statistic from T1S1) against the same three gene-set collections
Enrichment results report FDR-adjusted p-values, and any pathway resource that could not be located at run time is reported as a gap rather than silently skipped
Output includes a results table per gene-set collection and a summary dot/bar plot of top enriched pathways

plan.title: Muscle treated vs control DE (limma-trend) + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The data profile states the core facility delivered log2(TPM+1) normalized values, not raw counts, for 12000 genes across 12 muscle samples (6 treated, 6 control, unpaired, single batch). This rules out count-based negative-binomial models (DESeq2/edgeR) which require integer counts and their own size-factor normalization — applying them to already-log-normalized data would double-normalize and violate the count-distribution assumption. The correct approach for pre-normalized log-expression data, as established by Ritchie et al. 2015 (limma, Nucleic Acids Research) and Law et al., is limma's linear model with empirical Bayes moderation and the mean-variance trend option (limma-trend), which fits directly on log-expression values without a voom step (voom is only for converting raw counts to log-CPM with precision weights, which is not needed here since values are already log-scale and normalized). Track 1 performs sample-level QC (PCA, sample correlation) to confirm the profiled design (6v6, single batch, no unexpected outliers or batch structure), filters low-expressed genes, fits the limma-trend model for treated vs control, and outputs the full differential expression table plus diagnostic and volcano plots. Track 2 takes the resulting gene list/ranked statistic and tests it for pathway enrichment (ORA and GSEA) against three independent, organism-matched pathway resources confirmed present in the environment (WikiPathways human, MSigDB Hallmark human, Reactome pathways filtered to human), giving biological context to the DE result without overreaching into translational claims the data does not support (no drug identity, PK, or clinical outcome data were provided).
